posts.post_subject: How were the "Sri Yantra Inspired" holograms made?
posts.content_md:
I was looking at some amazing pictures of holograms by Fred Unterseher (

[http://www.physics.ohio-state.edu/~kaga ... _28Feb.pdf](http://www.physics.ohio-state.edu/~kagan/holo_show05/cat_holo_28Feb.pdf)

 about half way down). He calls it 'Off axis Fourier transform lens matrix holographic optical element'. Can someone take a shot at explaining to me how these were made? I've read Saxby and I know what Fourier transforms and holographic optical elements are, but how do you get those holograms? Are they computer generated?

 Thanks much,

 Dave

posts.topic_title: How were the "Sri Yantra Inspired" holograms made?
posts.author: dave battin
posts.post_subject: How were the "Sri Yantra Inspired" holograms made?
posts.content_md:
> **Thesrot:** 'Off axis Fourier transform lens matrix holographic optical element'. Can someone take a shot at explaining to me how these were made? Dave

Off axis Fourier transform-a hologram using a reference beam probably coming from above (and not straight on at 90 degrees to the plate).

lens matrix-the object ,a lens used a number of times,for multi objects ,hence (matrix)

holographic optical element-optical component to bend or control light.

that would be my take on the title and not done using a computer....

anyone else to give it a try ?
